 ## Prepare your local Java environment
 
+To get started using Spanner in your own application, add the client library to your project dependencies:
+
+> **Note:** If your application uses the Spring Framework, a [Spring Data module](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/adding-spring) is also available.
+
+If you are using [Maven](https://maven.apache.org/) , add the following to your `pom.xml` file. For more information about BOMs, see [The Google Cloud Platform Libraries BOM](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/bom) .
+
+```java
+<dependencyManagement>
+  <dependencies>
+    <dependency>
+      <groupId>com.google.cloud</groupId>
+      <artifactId>libraries-bom</artifactId>
+      <version>26.90.0</version>
+      <type>pom</type>
+      <scope>import</scope>
+    </dependency>
+  </dependencies>
+</dependencyManagement>
+
+<dependencies>
+  <dependency>
+    <groupId>com.google.cloud</groupId>
+    <artifactId>google-cloud-spanner</artifactId>
+  </dependency>
+</dependencies>
+```
+
+If you are using [Gradle](https://gradle.org/) , add the following to your dependencies:
+
+```java
+implementation platform('com.google.cloud:libraries-bom:26.90.0')
+
+implementation 'com.google.cloud:google-cloud-spanner'
+```
+
+If you are using [sbt](https://www.scala-sbt.org/) , add the following to your dependencies:
+
+```java
+libraryDependencies += "com.google.cloud" % "google-cloud-spanner" % "6.125.0"
+```
+
+If you're using Visual Studio Code or IntelliJ, you can add client libraries to your project using the following IDE plugins:
+
+- [Cloud Code for VS Code](https://docs.cloud.google.com/code/docs/vscode/client-libraries)
+- [Cloud Code for IntelliJ](https://docs.cloud.google.com/code/docs/intellij/client-libraries)
+
+The plugins provide additional functionality, such as key management for service accounts. Refer to each plugin's documentation for details.
+
+> **Note:** Cloud Java client libraries do not currently support Android.
+
+Alternatively, if you want to run the sample application used in this tutorial, follow these steps to prepare your local environment:
+
 1.  Install the following on your development machine if they are not already installed:
 
     - Java 8 JDK ( [download](http://openjdk.java.net/) ).

@@ -158,6 +158,8 @@ Calculates a relevance score of a `TOKENLIST` for a full-text search query. The
 
 The scorer algorithm is periodically updated. After a short evaluation period, the default behavior updates to the newest version. You are encouraged to leave the version unspecified so that your database can benefit from improvements to the scorer algorithm. However, you can set the version number in the `options` argument to retain old behavior. You can also use the `score_version` database option to set the default scorer version for your database. If the `version` parameter is present in a request, it overrides the `score_version` setting.
 
+When the scorer version updates, raw score values and the relative ranking order of search results can change. Paginated queries in flight at the moment of a version switch (where an earlier page uses one version and a later page uses another) might also experience a one-time discontinuity, such as dropped or repeated results; pagination started after the switch is consistent. Because scorer version updates are infrequent and any pagination discontinuity is transient, no action is needed for most applications. If necessary, you can use the `score_version` database option or the `version` parameter in the `SCORE` function's `options` argument to adopt a later version on your own schedule or temporarily retain an earlier version. However, leaving a version permanently pinned prevents your database from automatically receiving future scorer improvements.

+## October 30, 2026
+
+Feature
+
+Spanner supports equality and ordering comparisons on JSONB and JSON values. You can use these values in `GROUP_BY` and `ORDER BY` clauses without first converting them to another data type.
+
+In GoogleSQL, you can also convert other data types to `JSON` using `CAST(expression AS JSON)` and compare JSON values directly with non-JSON values. Spanner can implicitly coerces the non-JSON value to `JSON` for comparison.
+
+Additionally, you can use search indexes to accelerate equality comparisons such as `=` or `IN` on JSONB and JSON columns and subpaths.
+
+For more information, see [JSON comparison and sorting](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types#comparison_and_sorting) , [JSON comparison coercion](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/conversion_rules#json_comparison_coercion) , [CAST AS JSON](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/conversion_functions#cast_as_json) , [JSON search indexes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/full-text-search/json-indexes) , and [Working with JSONB](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/working-with-jsonb) .
